CLAUSE (2) "Every SM11 wall germ satisfying the central conditions of type T is a CV event" (excerpt 11). Lean lines 159–163: `∀ (g : WallGerm n) (e f k : ZMod n), g.TripleAt e f k → ∃ E : CV.Event n, E.radius = g.radius ∧ (∀ t hE hg, E.curve ⟨t,hE⟩ = g.curve ⟨t,hg⟩) ∧ ¬ CV.Generic g.center`.

The three functions are `edgeParameter P e f − edgeParameter P e k`, `edgeParameter P f e − edgeParameter P f k`, `edgeParameter P k e − edgeParameter P k f`, where `edgeParameter P i j = cramerFirst (P i) (P j) (edge i) (edge j) = det(P j − P i, edge j)/det(edge i, edge j)` (Chambers.lean:86, ContinuousGeometry.lean:18) — the Cramer solution s of P i + s·ℓ_i = P j + u·ℓ_j, i.e. SM's parameter t_{ij} on E_i (def:crossings, excerpt 260–268) — so on each of the three edges the difference of the two crossing parameters of the other two edges, exactly item (T) (excerpt 80–83; on-disk 762–765 verbatim). The sign of the difference is immaterial (`signChanges_sub_swap`). `TripleAt` is therefore the full printed item (T).
- "is a CV event": `CV.Event n` (CV/Events.lean:411–418): radius > 0, continuous curve on Ioo(−r,r) into `LabelledTuple n`, `IsPolygon` at the centre, `CV.Generic` for t ≠ 0, `¬ CV.Generic` at 0 = def:event (d1_setup 1072–1076) "continuous path of polygons on n vertices, t ∈ (−ε,ε), generic for every t ≠ 0 and P(0) not" (polygon at t ≠ 0 follows from `Generic.isPolygon`). Since `Event` bundles the map with the defining proofs, "g is a CV event" is exactly "∃ E : Event with E.radius = g.radius and E.curve = g.curve"; same radius fixes the same interval, and the pointwise identity over `t : ℝ` with both membership proofs (lines 161–162) is the correct rendering of equality of two functions whose subtype domains `Ioo(−E.radius) E.radius` and `Ioo(−g.radius) g.radius` are only propositionally equal — the header's explanation (lines 32–35) is accurate. The last conjunct `¬ CV.Generic g.center` restates the printed "P(0) is not generic" (already implied by E.nongeneric_center and the curve identity at t = 0); it adds nothing beyond the source and loses nothing.

SCOPE SENTENCE (excerpt 11, "restricted to that central type; it does not assert that every type of SM wall is a CV event"): the Lean quantifies clause (2) only over germs with `g.TripleAt e f k`; no clause mentions F/K/V/E/C germs and no claim is made about an arbitrary `WallGerm`. Matches exactly. The triple `e f k` is arbitrary (no e<f<g, no distinctness beyond what `TripleAt` forces), as in the printed B1 (§0's e<f<g convention is a naming convention consumed by B2's indexed members, not a hypothesis of B1); `TripleAt` is permutation-invariant (`tripleAt_support_iff`, UnorderedWallTriples.lean:80–83).

STANDING ASSUMPTIONS: `hn : 3 ≤ n` (line 157) is printed — SM def:polygon "Let n ≥ 3" (§0 line 48), CV def:polygon "Let n ≥ 3" (§0 line 80), SM_MAP "For n ≥ 3" (§0 line 33) — and is genuinely needed (for n = 1 `SM.Generic` is vacuous while `IsPolygon` fails). `[NeZero n]` (line 47) is not printed but is implied by 3 ≤ n and is forced by the library (`CV.rep`/`CV.Member`, `WallGerm.pointZeros` use `Finset.univ`); a redundant instance hypothesis, non-blocking.

No printed clause lacks a Lean counterpart and no Lean clause lacks a printed counterpart. Verdict: faithful; all discrepancies below are non-blocking.
discrepancies: non-blocking: `[NeZero n]` (statement file line 47) is an extra instance hypothesis not printed in Lemma B1; it is implied by the printed standing assumption `3 ≤ n` (SM/CV def:polygon 'Let n ≥ 3') and is required only because `CV.rep`/`CV.Member` and `WallGerm.pointZeros` are defined with `[NeZero n]`. No loss of generality.

non-blocking: the third conjunct `¬ CV.Generic g.center` (line 163) is redundant — it follows from `E.nongeneric_center` together with `E.radius = g.radius` and the pointwise curve identity at t = 0. It restates the printed def:event clause 'P(0) is not [generic]' rather than adding a new assertion.

non-blocking: 'the central conditions of type T' is formalised as the whole item (T) (`TripleAt`: Z_pt = ∅, Z_c = {{e,f,k}} AND the three parameter-difference sign changes). B1's own proof (excerpt 288–289) uses only Z_pt and Z_c; if the phrase were read as those two sets alone, the Lean hypothesis would be stronger than printed (see weaker_than_source). The reading adopted is the coherent one: §0 line 96 says B1 'transfers simple triple germs', and B2/B3 apply to 'the germ in B1' and need the sign changes.

non-blocking: `TripleAt` uses the total Cramer function `SM.edgeParameter` (Chambers.lean:86; = det(P j − P i, edge j)/det(edge i, edge j), Lean's x/0 = 0) where the printed (T) speaks of 'the two crossing parameters … (which exist on both sides by lem:triple-sides)'. Where the crossings exist the two agree (`crossingParameter_eq_edgeParameter`, `CV.crossParam_eq_edgeParameter`), and the sign-change condition is local, so the predicates coincide on type-T germs; this is a shape choice of the accepted def:walls module, not of this row.

non-blocking (provenance): the excerpt's SM11 line citations (def:germ 653–668, lem:triple-sides 670–675, (T) 735–738, lem:g1 110–123) do not match the on-disk reference/SM/sm-1-polygons.tex (SM15), where def:germ is 680–695, lem:triple-sides 697–702, (T) 762–765. The quoted texts of def:germ, lem:triple-sides and (T) are verbatim identical to the on-disk file; lem:g1 (ii)/(iv) wording differs slightly between the SM11 quote and SM15 (no bearing on the B1 statement).
stronger_than_source: None material. Clause (2) quantifies over every ordering of the central triple (`e f k : ZMod n` unconstrained, line 159) and states `¬ CV.Generic g.center` explicitly (line 163); both are already implied by the printed statement (B1 imposes no ordering; def:event contains the non-generic centre), so the Lean is equal in strength, not stronger.

Under the natural reading (the printed item (T), i.e. §0's 'simple triple germ') there is no weakening.

refuters.argument:
Not refuted. Clause-by-clause, the Lean `Bridge.B1` (statement file lines 157-163) matches BRIDGE.md B1 (excerpt lines 3-11) once all definitions are expanded to primitives; I found no clause where the Lean is stronger, and the only weaker reading is interpretive and non-blocking.

HYPOTHESES. (a) `hn : 3 ≤ n` is the printed standing assumption "Let n ≥ 3" of SM def:polygon and CV def:polygon (§0 context lines 48, 80); `[NeZero n]` is redundant given it (non-blocking). (b) `g : WallGerm n` (SM/WallGerm.lean:13-19): radius > 0, continuous curve on Set.Ioo(-r, r) → LabelledTuple n, SM.Generic for t ≠ 0, not SM.Generic at 0 — SM def:germ verbatim (excerpt lines 57-62). (c) `g.TripleAt e f k` (SM/NamedWallPredicates.lean:30-34) = `pointZeros = ∅ ∧ concurrences = {{e,f,k}} ∧` three `SignChanges`. `pointZeros = pointZeroTriples g.center` = the 3-element sets with chi = 0 (SM/ZeroTriples.lean:13-41; `pointZeroTriple_iff` gives χ_{ijk}=0 for distinct i,j,k) = Z_pt. `concurrences = concurrenceTriples g.center` = 3-sets, pairwise `remote` (= ¬adjacent, j−i ∈ {−1,0,1}, SM/Polygon.lean:63-66, identical to CV's Remote = ¬Consecutive), with a common point in the three `edgeInterior`s (ZeroTriples.lean:61-67) = Z_c. `edgeParameter P i j = cramerFirst (P i) (P j) (edge P i) (edge P j) = det(P j − P i, d_j)/det(d_i, d_j)` (SM/Chambers.lean:86, SM/ContinuousGeometry.lean:18); solving P i + s d_i = P j + r d_j gives exactly this s, i.e. SM's parameter t_{ij} ALONG E_i (confirmed by `CV.crossParam_eq_edgeParameter`, CV/Setup.lean:572, with CV's t_f along e). Hence the three clauses are t_{ef}−t_{ek} on E_e, t_{fe}−t_{fk} on E_f, t_{ke}−t_{kf} on E_k — exactly "on each of the three edges the two crossing parameters of the other two edges"; the sign convention of the difference is irrelevant to a sign change. `WallGerm.SignChanges φ` (SM/GermSignChange.lean:10-12) = ∃δ>0 (≤ radius) with φ(curve t)·φ(curve −t) < 0 for 0<t<δ (`sideTuple true/false` = curve(±t), WallGerm.lean:34-50) — SM's printed "changes sign at 0" (excerpt lines 70-71); `signChanges_iff_local` shows the δ ≤ radius bound is immaterial. On the small sides the crossings exist (lem:triple-sides), so the total Cramer function coincides with the printed crossing parameter there; no germ is added or lost.

CONCLUSION. `CV.Event n` (CV/Events.lean:411-418) = radius > 0, continuous curve into LabelledTuple n, `IsPolygon` at the centre, `CV.Generic` for t ≠ 0, `¬CV.Generic` at 0; `CV.Generic P = IsPolygon P ∧ ∀ m : Member n, m.Relevant P → m.eval P ≠ 0` (CV/Setup.lean:1051-1052), so every P(t) is a CV polygon — CV def:event ("a continuous path of polygons … generic for every t ≠ 0 and P(0) is not", excerpt lines 224-226). Because an `Event` is determined by (radius, curve) with the remaining fields propositions, `∃ E, E.radius = g.radius ∧ (∀ t hE hg, E.curve ⟨t,hE⟩ = g.curve ⟨t,hg⟩)` is exactly "the germ's map on (−ε, ε) is a CV event"; the extra `¬CV.Generic g.center` conjunct is implied (E.center = g.center by the pointwise identity at t = 0 plus `nongeneric_center`) and adds nothing. Same-radius is not a strengthening: the printed proof verifies CV-genericity at every punctured value of the original interval. Clause (1) `∀ P : LabelledTuple n, SM.Generic P → CV.Generic P`: `LabelledTuple n = ZMod n → Plane` is the common type, `edge P i = P(i+1) − P i` is d_i, p_i = μ_i is the identity map, so this is §0's labelled identification; `SM.Generic = G1 ∧ G2` (SM/Generic.lean:11-19) is SM def:generic; the `Member` index side-conditions (Setup.lean:638-643: G2 i∉{e,e+1}; G5 remote, ē<f̄; G3 pairwise remote, ē<f̄<ḡ; G4 f,g remote to e, f≠g, f̄<ḡ) and `Crosses` (remote ∧ two strict G2 products, Setup.lean:402-403) are d1_setup's printed families and activation.

STRENGTHENINGS CHECKED AND REJECTED: same radius (true on the full interval, as the printed proof shows); separate `¬CV.Generic g.center` (implied); `center_polygon` (printed "path of polygons"); any extra member or wrong indexing (B1 asserts nothing about the zero set); ordering of e f k (`TripleAt` is permutation-invariant, `tripleAt_support_iff`, UnorderedWallTriples.lean:80; B1 quantifies over all e f k anyway).

ONLY POSSIBLE WEAKENING (non-blocking, interpretive): Lean's `TripleAt` includes (T)'s sign-change clause, which BRIDGE's B1 proof (excerpt line 288) never uses. Under a reading of "the central conditions of type T" as only Z_pt = ∅ ∧ Z_c = {{e,f,g}}, a concrete even germ P(t) = P(0) + t²V (three edges concurrent at an interior point q at t = 0, separated for t ≠ 0, G1 throughout, hence φ(P(t)) = φ(P(−t)) and no sign change) would be covered by the printed text but not by the Lean. However §0 line 96 ("B1 transfers simple triple germs … The requested class inclusion is only from SM11 simple triple walls") and the sentence "restricted to that central type; it does not assert that every type of SM wall is a CV event" use "central type" for the wall type T as a whole, so the Lean's full-(T) hypothesis is the intended class; the content of the bridge (B2-B4 are about type-T germs) is unchanged.
